title: Conversation Archaeology Wave 014 — Composite Memory, City/Gate & Nested Door
purpose: Preserve older project-side material that becomes newly legible after the Bible reader and overlap census: distributed intertext memory, outside-gate/city topology, and recursive nested-Door structure. Recovery does not convert remembered wording into verified public quotation.

recovered_cluster: no lasting city / city to come
records.importance: Gate/city/perimeter material was already being explored months before the September circuit/perimeter synthesis. Hebrews 13's outside-gate→reproach→coming-city sequence therefore has an earlier project archaeology anchor than a purely September research date.
records.boundary: The recovered conversation was an interpretive exploration. It is not evidence that all listed texts describe one historical or prophetic event.

records.importance: The user was searching for a remembered composite rather than merely asking for Genesis 28. This is a concrete example of project memory that distributes one conceptual image across several canonical texts.

records.anchor: surely the Lord was in this place
records.correction: The user explicitly rejected Genesis 28 alone as the complete passage being sought.
records.importance: This correction should become a reader rule: when a remembered project composite exceeds one passage, preserve it as an intertext bundle instead of forcing one verse to carry every feature.

records.source_class: assistant reconstruction preserved only as conversation archaeology
candidate_text_family: cornerstone texts such as Psalms 118:22-23 / Gospel reuse
records.finding: No single canonical passage was identified that contains the entire remembered Ladder + Son-of-Man + angels/ascent + stone/cornerstone composite.
records.importance: This becomes the prototype for the archive's composite-memory/intertext-bundle data type.
records.boundary: The bundle is a research reconstruction, not a claim that biblical authors intended one hidden composite.

recovered_structure: Alpha hidden inside a smallest box and disguised as Omega
a Door inside a tiny box
records.key_formulation: every box potentially contains another Door
records.importance: Adds recursive/nested threshold topology: a Door need not only separate two macroscopic regions; a containing structure can reveal a further transition recursively. This can be modeled without claiming literal cosmological nesting.
records.boundary: Treat as project symbolic/system architecture. Do not present nested boxes or Doors as established physics.

new_methodological_result: The archive needs three textual-relation classes: single-passage relation, intertextual family, and project composite-memory bundle. A bundle should list which features belong to which texts and explicitly state when no one passage contains the whole remembered configuration.
